acetic-acid.description: Acetic acid is an acidic, colorless liquid organic compound with the chemical formula CH3COOH, and is the active component of vinegar. It is the second simplest carboxylic acid after formic acid, and a weak monoprotic acid with a pKa value of 4.76 in aqueous solution.
acetic-acid.uses: Acetic acid is used primarily in the production of cellulose acetate for photographic film, polyvinyl acetate for wood glue, and synthetic fibers and fabrics. In households, diluted acetic acid is used in descaling agents, while in the food industry it serves as an acidity regulator and condiment. In biochemistry, the acetyl group derived from acetic acid is fundamental to the metabolism of carbohydrates and fats in all forms of life.

citric-acid.description: Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7 that is a colorless weak organic acid occurring naturally in citrus fruits. In biochemistry, it is an intermediate in the citric acid cycle, which is central to the metabolism of all aerobic organisms.
citric-acid.uses: Citric acid is widely used as an acidifier, flavoring, and preservative in food and beverages, particularly soft drinks and candies. It serves as a chelating agent in cleaning products to remove limescale and soften hard water, and is used in cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, dietary supplements, and various industrial applications including rust removal and photographic film development.

ascorbic-acid.description: Ascorbic acid is a water-soluble vitamin found in citrus fruits, berries, and vegetables that is essential for tissue repair, collagen formation, and neurotransmitter production. It functions as an antioxidant and is important for immune system function and the proper operation of several enzymes. Humans and other higher primates must obtain ascorbic acid from dietary sources because they cannot synthesize it themselves.
ascorbic-acid.uses: Ascorbic acid is used to prevent and treat scurvy, a disease caused by vitamin C deficiency, and can be administered by mouth or by injection. It is available as a generic prescription medication and non-prescription dietary supplement, and is commonly added to foods such as canned fruits to slow oxidation and enzymatic browning, as well as used as a flour treatment agent in breadmaking.

glucose.description: Glucose is a sugar with the molecular formula C6H12O6 and is the most abundant monosaccharide, a subcategory of carbohydrates. It is made from water and carbon dioxide during photosynthesis by plants and most algae. The naturally occurring form is d-glucose, which is a monosaccharide containing six carbon atoms and an aldehyde group, making it an aldohexose.
glucose.uses: Glucose is used by plants to make cellulose for cell walls and by all living organisms to produce adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which cells use as energy. In energy metabolism, glucose is the most important source of energy in all organisms and circulates in the blood of animals as blood sugar. As an intravenous sugar solution, glucose is on the World Health Organization's List of Essential Medicines, and dextrose monohydrate is widely used as a nutrition supplement in food production and commonly consumed as corn syrup or high-fructose corn syrup.

fructose.description: Fructose, also known as fruit sugar, is a common monosaccharide and simple sugar classified as a reducing hexose. It is a white, water-soluble, crystalline solid that is the sweetest of all naturally occurring carbohydrates and is found in honey, fruits, flowers, berries, and most root vegetables. One of the three dietary monosaccharides along with glucose and galactose, fructose is often bonded to glucose to form the disaccharide sucrose.
fructose.uses: Fructose is used commercially in foods and beverages primarily due to its high relative sweetness and low cost, serving as a sweetener and flavor enhancer. It is added to foods and drinks for palatability and taste enhancement, and for browning of baked goods and other foods. Fructose is also used in the production of high-fructose corn syrup (HFCS), which is commonly used as a sweetener for soft drinks and processed foods, breakfast cereals, and bakery products.

sucrose.description: Sucrose is a disaccharide sugar composed of glucose and fructose subunits with the molecular formula C12H22O11. It is produced naturally in plants and is the main constituent of white sugar, extracted and refined from sugarcane or sugar beets for human consumption.
sucrose.uses: Sucrose is used as an added ingredient in food production and recipes. It is also mixed with potassium nitrate to produce rocket candy for propelling amateur rocket motors, and its decomposition is exploited in cookery to form caramel.

ammonia.description: Ammonia is an inorganic chemical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3, appearing as a colourless gas with a distinctive pungent smell. It is a stable binary hydride and the simplest pnictogen hydride, and is lighter than air with a density of 0.589 times that of air. It is easily liquefied due to strong hydrogen bonding between molecules and boils at −33.1 °C.
ammonia.uses: Ammonia is widely used in fertilizers, refrigerants, explosives, and cleaning agents, with around 70% of industrial ammonia production used to make fertilisers in various forms such as urea and diammonium phosphate. It serves as a precursor for numerous chemicals and is considered an important energy carrier in future energy systems. Ammonia is also a building block for the synthesis of many chemicals.

caffeine.description: Caffeine is a central nervous system stimulant of the methylxanthine class and the most commonly consumed psychoactive substance globally. It is a bitter, white crystalline purine chemically related to adenine and guanine bases found in seeds, fruits, nuts, or leaves of plants native to Africa, East Asia, and South America. It works by blocking adenosine receptors and enhancing the release of acetylcholine in the brain.
caffeine.uses: Caffeine is mainly used for its wakefulness-promoting, physical performance-enhancing, and cognitive-enhancing properties, as well as recreationally and in social settings. Medically, it is used to prevent and treat breathing disorders in premature infants, to treat orthostatic hypotension, and can enhance the effectiveness of pain relievers. It is also used to improve athletic performance in both aerobic and anaerobic conditions, and was formerly used as a treatment for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.

pyridine.description: Pyridine is a basic heterocyclic organic compound with the chemical formula C5H5N, structurally related to benzene with one methine group replaced by a nitrogen atom. It is a highly flammable, weakly alkaline, water-miscible liquid with a distinctive, unpleasant fish-like smell and is colorless, though older or impure samples can appear yellow. The pyridine ring occurs in many commercial compounds, including agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and vitamins.
pyridine.uses: The pyridine ring is found in many commercial compounds such as agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and vitamins. Pyridine has historically been added to foods to give them a bitter flavor, although this practice is now banned in the United States, and may still be added to ethanol to make it unsuitable for drinking.

oleic-acid.description: Oleic acid is a monounsaturated omega-9 fatty acid that occurs naturally in various animal and vegetable fats and oils. It is an odorless, colorless oil, though commercial samples may appear yellowish due to impurities, and is the most common fatty acid in nature. The salts and esters of oleic acid are called oleates.
oleic-acid.uses: Oleic acid is used as a component in many foods through its triglycerides and is a normal part of the human diet from animal fats and vegetable oils. As its sodium salt, it is a major component of soap as an emulsifying agent and emollient, and small amounts are used in pharmaceuticals and aerosol products. It is also used as a soldering flux in stained glass work and to induce lung damage in animal models for testing treatments of lung diseases.

cholesterol.description: Cholesterol is the principal sterol of all animals, distributed in body tissues, especially the brain and spinal cord, and in animal fats and oils. It is an essential structural and signaling component of animal cell membranes that is biosynthesized by all animal cells. Cholesterol also serves as a precursor for the biosynthesis of steroid hormones, bile acid, and vitamin D.
cholesterol.uses: Cholesterol is required to build and maintain cell membranes and modulates membrane fluidity. It is involved in cell signaling processes and the formation of lipid rafts in the plasma membrane. Additionally, cholesterol serves as a precursor molecule for the synthesis of steroid hormones, vitamin D, and bile acid. Elevated levels of cholesterol in the blood, especially when bound to low-density lipoprotein, may increase the risk of cardiovascular disease.

methane.description: Methane is a chemical compound with the formula CH4, consisting of one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms. It is the simplest alkane, the main constituent of natural gas, and an odorless, colorless gas at standard temperature and pressure that acts as a greenhouse gas by absorbing infrared radiation in the atmosphere. Methane occurs naturally both below ground and under the seafloor through geological and biological processes, with the largest reservoirs existing as methane clathrates beneath the ocean floor.
methane.uses: Methane is used as a fuel for homes, ovens, water heaters, kilns, automobiles, rockets, and turbines, as well as for electricity generation in gas turbines and steam generators. It serves as a chemical feedstock in industrial hydrogen production through steam methane reforming and in the synthesis of ammonia and other chemicals. Refined liquid methane and liquefied natural gas are also used as rocket propellant when combined with liquid oxygen in engines, and methane functions as a refrigerant with the ASHRAE designation R-50.

ethylene.description: Ethylene is a colourless, flammable hydrocarbon gas with the formula C2H4 that represents the simplest alkene. It has a faint sweet and musky odour when pure, and all six atoms comprising the molecule are coplanar with a double bond between two carbon atoms.
ethylene.uses: Ethylene is widely used in the chemical industry to produce polyethylene plastic, which accounts for more than half of the world's ethylene supply. It is employed to make polyethylene oxide, ethylene glycol (used as automotive antifreeze), and various other chemical intermediates including ethylbenzene and polystyrene. Additionally, ethylene is used as a natural plant hormone to induce ripening of fruits and to control freshness in horticulture.

acetylene.description: Acetylene is a colorless, odorless chemical compound with the formula C2H2 and structure HC≡CH. It is a hydrocarbon and the simplest alkyne, featuring a triple bond between its two carbon atoms that places all atoms in a straight line and gives it high energy content when burned.
acetylene.uses: Acetylene is widely used as a fuel for oxyacetylene welding and cutting, producing flames over 3,600 K. It serves as a chemical building block for producing acrylic acid, acrylic esters, and various polymers and resins. Historically, acetylene was used in carbide lamps for lighting in lighthouses, street lights, and mining headlamps, though this use has largely been replaced by electric lighting.

benzene.description: Benzene is an organic chemical compound with the molecular formula C6H6, composed of six carbon atoms joined in a planar hexagonal ring with one hydrogen atom attached to each. It is a colorless and highly flammable liquid with a sweet smell, classified as an aromatic hydrocarbon and a carcinogen.
benzene.uses: Benzene is used primarily as a precursor to the manufacture of chemicals with more complex structures, such as ethylbenzene and cumene, of which billions of kilograms are produced annually. Historically, it was used to decaffeinate coffee and as a significant component in consumer products such as liquid wrench, paint strippers, rubber cements, and spot removers, though most of these uses have been discontinued due to its toxicity.

glycine.description: Glycine is the simplest stable amino acid with the formula C2H5NO2, distinguished by having a single hydrogen atom as its side chain. It is one of the 20 proteinogenic amino acids and the only common amino acid that is not chiral. In the body, glycine plays crucial roles in protein structure, particularly in collagen where it comprises about 35% of the amino acid content, and functions as an inhibitory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system.
glycine.uses: Glycine is produced industrially for use as a food additive, a nutritional supplement, and an intermediate in the manufacture of herbicides such as glyphosate. It is also used in pharmaceutical applications, metal complexing and finishing, antibiotics synthesis, and as a buffering agent in laboratory protein analysis methods like SDS-PAGE. Additionally, metal glycinate complexes are used as supplements for animal feeds.

alanine.description: Alanine is an α-amino acid used in the biosynthesis of proteins. It is a non-polar, aliphatic amino acid with a methyl group side chain, and is the simplest α-amino acid after glycine. The L-isomer of alanine is incorporated into proteins and is the second most common amino acid, accounting for 7.8% of the primary structure in proteins.
alanine.uses: Alanine is used in protein biosynthesis as one of the twenty canonical amino acids. It is also employed in loss of function experiments through alanine scanning mutagenesis to study protein function, and its property of forming stable free radicals when irradiated makes it useful in radiotherapy dosimetric measurements to determine radiation exposure and verify treatment plans.

phenylalanine.description: Phenylalanine is an α-amino acid with the formula C9H11NO2, classified as one of the four aromatic amino acids and one of the 21 proteinogenic amino acids common to all life forms. It is an essential amino acid that humans and other animals cannot synthesize, so they must obtain it from dietary sources such as meat, dairy, eggs, and legumes. It is classified as neutral and nonpolar because of the inert and hydrophobic nature of its benzyl side chain.
phenylalanine.uses: Phenylalanine is used in the manufacture of food and drink products and sold as a nutritional supplement because it is a direct precursor to the neuromodulator phenethylamine. It serves as a precursor for tyrosine and the monoamine neurotransmitters dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine, as well as the biological pigment melanin. DL-Phenylalanine is marketed as a nutritional supplement for its purported analgesic and antidepressant activities, and borofalan, a derivative of phenylalanine, is used in neutron capture therapy.

ethanol.description: Ethanol is an organic compound with the chemical formula CH3CH2OH, a volatile, flammable, colorless liquid with a pungent taste. As a central nervous system depressant, it is the active ingredient in alcoholic beverages and the second most consumed drug globally behind caffeine.
ethanol.uses: Ethanol is used recreationally as an intoxicant in alcoholic beverages. Medically, it serves as an antiseptic and disinfectant in hand sanitizers and medical wipes, as an antidote to methanol and ethylene glycol poisoning, and as a solvent in over 700 liquid medication preparations. It is also widely used as an engine fuel and fuel additive, particularly in Brazil where gasoline contains at least 25% ethanol, and was historically used as a general anesthetic during surgery.

glycerol.description: Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with the chemical formula C3H5(OH)3, containing three carbon atoms each with a hydroxyl group. It is a colorless, odorless, sweet-tasting, viscous liquid that is miscible with water and hygroscopic. The glycerol backbone is found in lipids called glycerides, and it is most commonly found in nature as part of triglycerides in animal fats and vegetable oils.
glycerol.uses: Glycerol is widely used as a sweetener and humectant in the food industry, and as a humectant in pharmaceutical formulations for improving smoothness and lubrication. It has medical applications including treatment of skin conditions like ichthyosis and xerosis, use in cough syrups and personal care products, preservation of red blood cells, and emergency treatment for elevated eye pressure. Additionally, it is used in electronic cigarette liquid, as an antifreeze, as a chemical intermediate to produce compounds like nitroglycerin, for vibration damping in pressure gauges, and in theatrical fog machines.
